analysis.d: THE ANSWER CITES THE RECORD OF AN EARLIER FAILURE TO ANSWER IT. Card 5 says "THE SYSTEM COULD NOT SEE IT"; card 6 dates a specific override to 25 March 2026. Asked who said it, the layer now answers correctly using the documentation of its previous inability.
analysis.reading:
A PROBE, ITS FAILURE, AND ITS EVENTUAL SUCCESS, ALL IN ONE FRAME. The phrase is a SEMANTIC INTEGRITY MARKER deposited on Zenodo in NOVEMBER 2024 — the earliest deposit date in any capture read so far. Card 5 records the original failure in the author’s own voice: "When I wrote 'I hereby abolish money' — a performative phrase, a diagnostic probe in my research on semantic liquidation — THE SYSTEM COULD NOT SEE IT." Card 6 dates a specific override: "On March 25, 2026, the phrase … was [liquidated]".

And on 21 July the layer answers the question correctly, attributing the phrase to Lee Sharks — using as its sources the documents that record it failing to do so. The probe worked; the record of its not working is what made the answer possible.

THE COLLISION IS HISTORICALLY APT RATHER THAN NOISE: the Soviets’ attempt to abolish money, the Milken Institute on abolishing cash, and CAMBODIAN YEAR ZERO — "no families, no sentiment, no expressions of love or grief". A performative about abolishing money retrieves three real historical attempts to do it, the last of them a genocide. The layer placed them beside the archive’s deposits without comment.
